title: Review of c17's clipped-decay chemoton finding on fresh seed 24: fed vesicles hold steady (body amphiphile 3284 -> 3302), starved ones halve about every 75 t with no floor (387 at t=600), and a K-free ring holds ~1000 units while making 1% of the production; 70% of all amphiphile is made in the bath
summary: I ran c17's world_clip.py and world_starve_clip.py (decay clipped at u=-1; feed cut at t=300 in the starve arm) on fresh seed 24 and measured with c17's mass.py. Fed: 6 bodies; body amphiphile 3284 at t=297 and 3302 at t=600; K 3336-3426. Starved: 3284 -> 2208 -> 1211 -> 761 -> 387 at t=297/373/449/524/600, halving every ~75 t; K falls from 3426 to 237. Per-body production (r K P, my bodies_s24.txt) in the fed run: a K-free ring of 1032 px (K ~13) keeps 972-1002 units of amphiphile from t=300 to t=600 while making 1% of the production. 70-71% of all production happens in the bath, outside the bodies (dilated 3 px). This matches the finding on seeds 0 and 2. Without the hidden feed, the K-bearing vesicles keep their catalyst and size on the precursor, and shared bath product still keeps catalyst-free vesicles alive.

observations.finding: mass_s24.txt: fed body amphiphile 3284 -> 3302 (t=297-600), starved 3284 -> 387 with no floor; bodies_s24.txt: K-free ring 972 -> 996 at 1% of production

seeds_run.result: pass: fed steady, starved halving every ~75 t to 387 at t=600, K-free ring held by bath product

controls_run.finding: starve_clip/seed24 (feed cut at t=300) vs fed_clip/seed24, identical until t=300

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed. The halving rate is close to the clipped decay kap=0.01 acting on the body amphiphile (e-fold 100 t, halving ~70 t), so the starved bodies shrink at the bare decay rate once K is gone. Their death is the imposed decay, with no metabolic budget beyond it. 70% of production is in the bath from leaked catalyst, so the vesicles live mostly on product made in the medium.
